title: 2D rest machining: Pocket and Adaptive cut only what a larger previous tool left

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat), after a feature comparison with the open-source project stevecad/camlib: "We wanna cover some of the toolpaths and things like that at first." and, on the suggested picks: "Lets create issues on your suggestions, they made sense." On sources: "We should use perplexity to find literature on those types of toolpaths and not copy them straight up".

What is missing: rest machining exists for 3D operations, but a 2D Pocket (and 2D Adaptive) cannot be limited to what a larger previous tool left: a small finishing tool re-cuts the whole pocket in air.

Wanted: on 2D Pocket and 2D Adaptive, a "Rest machining" group: on/off, source (previous tool diameter and corner radius entered by hand, or "from the previous operations" using the carried stock), and a rest allowance. The path covers only the regions the previous tool could not reach (corners, narrow necks), entered from already cut space where there is any.

Safety: the rest region must be a superset of the material really left. Under-reading it leaves a full-width cut for a small tool, which breaks it. With the hand-entered source the op says in its summary that it trusts the entered tool; with the carried-stock source the regions are checked against the stock simulation in a test.

Sources: step one of the work is a literature search (Perplexity) for published material on 2D rest-region computation (offset differences, medial-axis reach of a tool); the code is written from that and named in the provenance comment. camlib is a feature list only: no code is copied or adapted from it.

Done means: a pocket with 3 mm corners roughed by a 12 mm tool gets a rest pass with a 4 mm tool that cuts only the corners (golden CL); simulation shows no passes over cleared floor and no plunge into uncut stock; undo/redo; MCP parameters; a previous tool smaller than the current one is refused by name; the literature used is cited in the PR.
